comparator.name: Notarial Law
comparator.sourceNotes: The catalogue introduces the revision by cohort from September 2025. This partial record shows its first two years. Year one requires 60 EC, plus the zero-credit Leiden Law Practices activities. Year two has 45 EC compulsory, a 5 EC technology and law choice and 10 EC of notarial electives. The first eligible technology and law option is shown. Year two builds on the first-year private, European and administrative law courses. The displayed third year is for 2024 and earlier entrants. The revised third year is announced for the 2027–2028 catalogue.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s Notarial Law degree introduces several areas of law and develops specialist study of property, family and company law. Students learn to analyze legal problems and build legal arguments.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The table shows the first two years of the revised degree. Leiden’s current catalogue lists the earlier curriculum for year three, so the full comparison remains under review.

curriculum.limitation: The verified first two years total 120 EC, including 15 EC of year-two choices. The revised third-year courses and thesis requirements are still under review. First-year Leiden Law Practices activities carry no credits.
